title: Sequential Mirror program over one shared block
hypothesis: Reusing one learned 2x2 physical block at two sequential depths with separate one-angle Givens Views will approximate held-out noncommuting two-block linear functions with at least 25% lower actual N=20 payload and no more than 10% relative NRMSE penalty versus two independent blocks.
physical_object: one learned 2x2 matrix W reused at both sequential steps
mirror_coordinate: per-step Givens angle theta_1, theta_2; step map is R(theta_s)W
logical_multiplicity: two ordered logical functions/steps from one physical matrix
controls: two independent 2x2 blocks / Routing Networks upper control
shared W plus per-step rank-one residuals

task.teacher: A_s=R(phi_s)S(k_s), S(k)=[[1,k],[0,1]]; independently sampled angles and shears
task.noncommuting_audit: report mean ||A2A1-A1A2||_F and order-swapped query NRMSE

development.selection: fixed Adam lr=0.03, 500 updates; no fresh tuning

paid_objects: all learned W or step matrices

success_gate: Every fresh world has Mirror NRMSE <=1.10x independent blocks and N20 Mirror actual payload <=0.75x independent payload; Mirror must be better than tied baseline on all worlds.
failure_gate: Any per-world quality gate misses, Mirror is not better than tied, N20 payload ratio exceeds 0.75, or order-sensitivity audit shows teacher is effectively commuting.
boundaries: No nonlinear or natural task evidence.
Private rank-one residual is a simple control and may exceed independent storage; report honestly.
amendment_A1: The first fresh screening initialized both factors of the rank-one residual control at zero, making the bilinear factors gradient-dead. Excluded initial worlds 45510-45512 as exploratory and froze a nonzero factor initialization before replacement worlds.
